🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict
This looks like a known, already-analysed Izenda reporting slowness problem in our own code, with performance fixes written but switched off for each client until enabled; it is not a Tailored Brands data problem. I can't confirm from here that those fixes are enabled for this client.

What we checked

  • The client notes for Tailored Brands have nothing on reporting slowness, and the cross-client incident list has no matching entry.

  • The client's configuration files have no reporting-related settings, so nothing there is client-specific to this report tool.

  • An existing engineering write-up covers the same symptoms: slow report pages, timeouts and "server side" errors after the move to shared hosting.

  • The performance fixes from that write-up are switched off by default per client, so they change nothing until someone turns them on for that client.

  • The write-up records an open mismatch where users see a timeout at roughly two minutes while the underlying query keeps running for up to ten minutes. That fits "times out, then blank page, retry".

  • A separate setting can send this report tool to its own dedicated server. That setting is off by default after an earlier outage.

Next

  • Check whether the two Izenda performance settings and the dedicated-server routing setting are on or off for Tailored Brands in production.

  • Ask the customer for a few timestamps of slow or failed loads, so they can be matched against server logs and query times.

Escalating to Secure Engineering. On 16 October J.R. asked for engineering review of this ticket and customer priority treatment. He did not ask for a fix date.

1. Correction

Izenda reporting and the blank Security ID defect in https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-29451 are separate tracks. No common root cause is demonstrated. The twenty minute and one hour waiting times mentioned on the 16 October call followed a discussion of Ahold. They are not TBI measurements.

2. Environment and steps to reproduce

Environment: Production. Tailored Brands, Client ID 209, tenant tbi.

Database: sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform\nPath:     /tailoredbrands/nettrack/AdHoc/reportlist.aspx\n

Tailored Brands (TBI), reported 14 October 2026 by Colton Neal

  1. Open /tailoredbrands/nettrack/AdHoc/reportlist.aspx through an authenticated Incident session.

  2. Open Open Investigations with its saved filters. Record the filter values. The failing run's full values are unavailable.

  3. Try the Excel export.

  4. Edit the September cases report to Fiscal October, 4 to 31 October 2026. The customer calls it 2026 Cases by Month. The timeout URL identifies Cases MTD September. The saved report identity is unconfirmed.

Expected: the list, the report and the export complete without errors. No target duration is documented.

Actual: the list takes 2 to 5 minutes and a report another 2 to 4. Users see blank pages after the error, failed exports and server errors. Source: https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-29060?focusedCommentId=3396117

Screenshots on https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-29060: image-20261014-154021.png shows the server error. image-20261014-160957.png shows HTTP 524 at 2026-10-14 16:07:16 UTC.

The Talos triage and Claude proposed the flag lead and extracted the evidence. I reviewed the Jira history, the original screenshots and the 16 October call with J.R. and Matt myself. I ran no new timed production reproduction and collected no server trace. I have not read the effective flag values or request level timings. Could Engineering evaluate the flag lead?

Conversations outside the ticket: the 16 October call with Tailored and the internal call with J.R. and Matt. Matt considered the screenshots sufficient for Izenda review. He also said TBI feels slower than other clients. That is an impression, not a measurement.

5. Ruled out so far

Hypothesis

🤖 Talos triage · confidence: low

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict
Not enough to call this a Secure bug yet. The ticket only lists examples of users with no security ID in their profile, and the attached files can't be read here. No known or recurring incident matches.

What we checked

  • A user's "security ID" in Incident is stored on the user record. It is set at account creation and sign-in, or by an admin security-level assignment, so each affected user needs checking individually.

  • When a user signs in through single sign-on, the ID comes from the sign-in provider or an admin assignment. If neither supplies one, the user keeps whatever value they already had, which is 0 for a new account. Only Appriss and Trebu email addresses are forced to a fixed ID.

  • The client's notes and the shared known-incidents list have nothing on missing security IDs. The only Tailored Brands pattern listed is the cancelled-transaction one, which is unrelated.

  • I couldn't tell from the ticket whether these users sign in through single sign-on or with a local password. That changes where to look.

Next

  • Compare the affected users in Colton's files against the live data. Check how each one signs in, whether their security ID is blank or 0, and whether an admin security-level assignment exists for them.

  • Ask Colton when the IDs were last correct for these users, and whether anything changed on their side (sign-in provider group mappings, a new user import, a migration to platform login).

Supplementing the existing Secure Engineering investigation. Colton supplied follow-up files for RCS-29451 and ENG-10069. Do not treat this follow-up as proof of a separate defect or create a duplicate engineering issue automatically.

1. Correction

Talos could not read the attachments or recover the prior investigation. Its lack of a matching precedent does not invalidate the published Rachel evidence. Matt has now posted the SSO+ process in the meeting chat, as supplied by Juan. His written explanation is no longer pending.

2. Environment and steps to reproduce

Environment: Production. Tailored Brands, Client ID 209, tenant tbi.

Database: sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform\nUI: Portal > Settings > Users > Secure Incident\nSource: Appriss Incident Security ID Examples.xlsx

Customer examples supplied 16 October 2026

  1. Open Jacinta Titus, Emeldia Pryor, Christi Winters, Rahim Mehdiyev or Cheneria Chevalier under Users.

  2. Open Secure Incident and inspect Incident Security ID.

  3. Compare the user with the supplied teams, permissions and locations files, then the effective SSO+ level and account state.

Expected: the configured level applies when the user signs in through SSO.

Actual: all five profiles show no selected level in the workbook screenshots. This is attachment evidence, not a fresh production reproduction. A last-login timestamp does not establish account creation or a first-login failure.

3. Findings

Source: the three appriss_sso_*_20261014*.csv attachments and the workbook on RCS-29469. Inspected all 29 embedded images. The workbook's empty cells do not mean its image-based evidence is empty.

Matt's written process: customer teams CSV contains email and team. The loader truncates and reloads sso.teams, looks up team text to a numeric securityid and replicates to sso.SecurityLevelAssignments. Expected output is one row per user, used at SSO login. This documents intended behavior; no TRUNCATE or production repair was executed during this investigation.

Chris: locations CSV line 301 contains Brand=SSU, Location=2005. The earlier SSO+ row held 90002005, dated 13 October. The supplied CSV is dated 14 October. It does not contain that literal code for Chris. Match the consumed batch before attributing the prefix's origin. Colton confirmed 40002005 as the correct location; Juan manually assigned it. Successful incident creation after that correction still needs confirmation.

Empty locations: 111 rows have no Location, all in teams other than Location Manager. Validate intended regional, district or administrative hierarchy before declaring these invalid store assignments.

4. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

Crosschecked the original CSVs, workbook images, previous SQL and Grafana findings, Ryan's Teams replies and the 16 October call with Matt and J.R. AI assisted extraction and drafting. No fresh production account check, loader trace or controlled login test was executed in this review.

The published Rachel timeline records level 5 before account creation, followed by a NULL account SecurityID while groups and team applied. Her next login preserved a manual correction; it does not prove automatic second-login recovery.

Conversations outside Jira: Ryan's 15 October Teams replies, the customer call and the internal Matt/J.R./Juan call on 16 October, plus Matt's subsequent written SSO+ explanation supplied by Juan. No direct permalink to that final chat message was provided. Ryan said it appears we add the 9; Matt requested the original file. The precise transformation remains unverified.

The historical security-level insertion timestamp was 13 October. Matt mentioned inserts on the 15th without a recoverable table name. Neither a successful replication task nor a filename establishes which file reached SSO+.

5. Ruled out so far

Interpretation

Evidence limit

Five users absent from the supplied files

They are present with Location Manager and ApprissCase Users. Ingestion and application still require validation.

All five are first-login failures

Their creation and login sequences have not all been established.

A second login or replacing 9 with 4 fixes everyone

Neither is a validated general remedy. Store numbers can occur under multiple brands.

Adding Security ID to the locations file is an approved workaround

Matt rejected it as a simple fix and described the existing teams-based implementation.

6. Still open

  1. Compare CSV, sso.teams, text-to-ID lookup, sso.SecurityLevelAssignments and account state at login for the five examples. Preserve ingestion and login timestamps.

  2. Check Matt's expected row count. Clarify how historical and manual Persistent rows interact with the one-row expectation before calling extra rows defective.

  3. Confirm ENG-10069 coverage for existing accounts such as Christi; append validated examples to the existing investigation.

  4. Trace Chris's SSU+2005 through the loader for the same batch, and confirm the corrected account can create an incident.

  5. Identify the exact table and query behind Matt's 15 October observation. Support's published offer of manual level assistance remains the recorded workaround. No bulk correction is approved.
